episodes.168016: As an upper-level ridge built over New Mexico on May 27, 2022, mid-level moisture seeping into the area underneath this ridge resulted in high based shower activity developing during the afternoon and evening hours. With very high mixing heights and dry surface conditions, any precipitation that fell out of these showers mainly evaporated and produced virga and strong dry microburst winds. Both the Albuquerque and Clines Corners ASOS stations measured downburst wind gusts in excess of 58 mph. Meanwhile, a dust devil was spotted in southwest Albuquerque, but it did no damage.
episodes.168247: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms spawned by a strong cold front produced hail, scattered damaging wind gusts, and a couple of tornadoes.
episodes.168248: Multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms spawned by a strong cold front produced hail, scattered damaging wind gusts, and a couple of tornadoes.
episodes.168255: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms produced strong to severe wind gusts over the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.168522: A thunderstorm became severe in northwestern Lawrence County and tracked east-southeast across the northern Black Hills and into parts of the west central South Dakota plains before weakening. The storm initially produced large hail to ping pong ball size and then strong wind gusts as it moved onto the plains.
episodes.168525: A thunderstorm briefly became severe as it passed east of the Rapid City area and across eastern Pennington County. Wind gusts to 65 mph were recorded in some areas from east of Rapid City to Wasta.
episodes.168526: A cluster of thunderstorms briefly became severe over parts of Jackson County, with some wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.168527: A thunderstorm briefly became severe in the Philip area, producing a few wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.168529: A line of severe thunderstorms developed over portions of central Campbell County and tracked northeast through much of Crook County. The storms mostly produced wind gusts over 70 mph, but were also accompanied by small hail.
episodes.168530: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked northeast from northeastern Wyoming and expanded east-northeast across northwestern South Dakota. Wind gusts to 65 mph were recorded across portions of the area.
episodes.168531: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked east-northeast across Bennett and Todd Counties. Hail around quarter size and eventually wind gusts around 70 mph accompanied the storm before it weakened over eastern Todd County.
episodes.168682: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeastern Colorado and moved into Perkins county. Though no large hail or damaging winds were reported, there was a landspout tornado which briefly touched down south of Grant.
episodes.168684: Thunderstorms developed just east of the Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of May 28th. As these storms tracked east, they increased in intensity and coverage as they entered the Nebraska Sandhills and portions of southwestern Nebraska. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported in Keith county.
episodes.169712: A phenomenon known as a heat burst occurred 9 miles north-northwest of Waka, TX. This occurs when anvil rains from dissipating showers/thunderstorms cause hot dry air loft to sink to the surface through somewhat of a dry downburst process leading to severe wind gust. In this case a mesonet station recorded a 79 mph wind wind gust.
episodes.169722: A strong cold front, in advance of a slow moving upper level low pressure system, brought multiple rounds of severe storms to southwest Virginia. With increasing instability and high low level shear, these storms produced damaging winds, hail and two tornadoes. While most of the severe weather occurred during the morning hours of the 27th, a second round of storms produced damaging winds during the afternoon.
episodes.169978: A nearly stationary frontal boundary remained across the Saint John Valley from the 27th into the 28th. The front served as a focus for heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms through the overnight hours of the 27th into the morning of the 28th. Along the Saint John Valley of northeast Aroostook county...rainfall totals from the overnight hours of the 27th into the morning of the 28th generally ranged from 3.00 to 4.50 inches with local totals in excess of 5.00 inches. In some areas...2.00 to 3.00 inches of rain fell in less than 4 hours during the early morning hours of the 28th. The heavy rains led to localized flash flooding which persisted into the late morning of the 28th. Several roads were closed due to rapidly flowing water including Little Madawaska Lake Road...Saint Marys Brook Road and West Road. The cemetary was flooded in the town of Van Buren. A beaver dam collapsed...releasing water which had impounded behind the dam. The surge of water from the release overwhelmed a culvert which led to a washout and total collapse of a portion of Route 1 near Cyr Plantation. The road was closed for nearly a month while repairs were completed.

episodes.170009: Several rounds of thunderstorms moved along a warm front of an approaching low pressure system on May 27th and into the 28th. These thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall over Northeast New Jersey resulting in several rounds of localized flash flooding. Several rounds of rainfall each with 0.75 to 1 inch of rain in an hour cause brief localized flash flooding. Total rainfall amounts in Northeast NJ were 1.5 to 3 inches.

An EF-1 tornado with winds estimated at 90 MPH touched down near the Saint Mary's and Charles County line between MD-5 Leonardtown Road and MD-231 Prince Frederick Road. The tornado tracked from around Charlotte Hall to near Benedict during the evening of Friday, May 27, 2022.||The tornado damage path started along Bach Drive, where a few trees were down and one tree was snapped about midway up. The tornado tracked across Charlotte Hall and MD-5 Leonardtown Road where damage was sporadic with a few trees down.||Damage became more concentrated around Mount Wolf Road, particularly around White Drive. Approximately one to two dozen trees were uprooted along White Drive along with a few trees being snapped. Large tree branches fell onto a house along White Drive causing damage to the siding along with broken windows. However, no other structural damage was noted in this area. Winds were estimated to be|around 90 mph across this area due to the uprooted large trees along with some large trees being snapped. Most of the tree damage was facing southwest to northeast, but there were a few trees that were facing west to east.||The tornado continued to track northeast causing tree damage along Chappelear Drive around Mount Wolf Road. Damage was more sporadic across this area, but a large softwood tree was uprooted and a tree fell onto a house. Witness statements along|with the survey noted that most of the damage on Chappelear Drive was around two or three houses. Most of the trees were facing south to north, which when compared to the location of the damage along White Road, shows counterclockwise rotation.||Damage to the north and east was sporadic, but there were several|areas that could not be accessed to survey. The tornado continued into Charles County.
